"Project: 2D Monster Catcher RPG

Create a complete 2D Monster Catcher RPG with an original fantasy world, original monsters, exploration, monster capturing, training, evolution, and turn-based combat.

1. Game Style

- 2D top-down RPG.
- Pixel art visual style.
- Smooth character movement and animations.
- Large interconnected world.
- Support PC and mobile controls.
- Responsive UI.

2. World Exploration

Create an explorable world containing multiple biomes:

- Greenwood Forest
- Ember Volcano
- Frozen Mountains
- Crystal Desert
- Shadow Swamp
- Ancient Ruins
- Dragon Valley
- Celestial Island

Each biome must have unique monsters, resources, NPCs, quests, and environmental designs.

3. Monster System

Create a monster database containing at least 50 original monsters initially.

Every monster must have:

- Unique ID and name.
- Sprite and animations.
- Element and rarity.
- Level and experience.
- HP, Attack, Defense, Speed, Special Attack and Special Defense.
- Skills and passive abilities.
- Evolution stages.
- Capture difficulty.
- Biome spawn information.

4. Catching System

- Wild monsters appear in the world.
- Start encounters when the player interacts with or approaches wild monsters.
- Allow the player to weaken monsters.
- Use capture items to catch monsters.
- Calculate capture probability using HP, rarity, status effects and capture item quality.
- Show capture animations and feedback.
- Add a monster storage system.

5. Combat System

Implement turn-based combat with:

- Attack.
- Skills.
- Monster switching.
- Items.
- Escape from wild battles.
- Elemental strengths and weaknesses.
- Critical hits.
- Status effects.
- Experience and rewards.

Allow the player to carry six monsters in the active party.

6. Evolution System

- Monsters can evolve into stronger forms.
- Add level-based evolution.
- Add item-based evolution.
- Add friendship-based evolution.
- Add location-based evolution.
- Evolution changes appearance, stats and abilities.
- Allow multiple evolution paths where appropriate.

7. Progression

Implement:

- Monster leveling.
- Experience rewards.
- Skill unlocking.
- Passive abilities.
- Monster personalities.
- Quests and achievements.
- Trainer progression.

8. Additional Systems

- Pokédex.
- Monster storage.
- Inventory.
- Crafting.
- Breeding.
- NPC trainers.
- Regional boss monsters.
- Day and night cycle.
- Save and load system.

9. UI

Create polished interfaces for:

- Main menu.
- Party.
- Monster details.
- Monster storage.
- Pokédex.
- Inventory.
- Map.
- Quest journal.
- Battle screen.
- Settings.

10. Development Requirements

- Use modular, maintainable code.
- Separate monster data from gameplay logic.
- Use reusable monster and battle systems.
- Avoid duplicating code.
- Implement proper collision detection.
- Ensure smooth movement and transitions.
- Save player progress persistently.
- Make all buttons and gameplay systems functional.

IMPORTANT:
Do not create just a visual prototype. Build actual playable systems with working interactions, progression, and persistent game data.

Start by creating the core playable prototype: player movement, a small explorable map, wild monster encounters, monster catching, party management, and turn-based battles. Test each system before expanding the game.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

No package.json, so plain HTML project (type 'html'). The start script serves static root. We should build static HTML/JS/CSS with no build step ideally. Use vanilla JS ES modules, canvas-based rendering with pixel art generated procedurally (since no external assets) or SVG sprites. Need a large game. Key requirements:

- 2D top-down pixel art
- 8 biomes interconnected
- 50+ original monsters with sprites/animations, elements, rarity, stats, skills, passives, evolution, capture difficulty, biome spawns
- Catching, battles, party, storage, evolution, progression, pokedex, inventory, crafting, breeding, NPC trainers, bosses, day/night, save/load, quest journal, achievements
- UI polished, responsive, PC + mobile controls
- Functional systems and persistence

Big task. Strategy: build a well-structured vanilla JS game with canvas. Generate monster pixel sprites procedurally from deterministic seeded palettes/shapes so 50+ unique-looking monsters with animation (idle bob, blink, attack lunge) via canvas. Tile-based overworld with biomes regions in one large map, smooth movement. Implement all systems with real data.

Let me plan architecture:

- index.html
- styles.css
- src/main.js — boot, game loop, screens
- src/data/monsters.js — 60+ monsters, evolution chains
- src/data/skills.js
- src/data/items.js
- src/data/quests.js
- src/data/biomes.js
- src/data/dialogue.js / npcs
- src/engine/state.js — save/load, state
- src/engine/monster.js — stat calc, xp, evolution, breeding
- src/engine/battle.js — turn-based battle engine
- src/engine/capture.js
- src/engine/world.js — map generation, movement, collision, encounters
- src/render/sprites.js — procedural pixel sprite generation
- src/render/worldRenderer.js
- src/ui/*.js — HUD, screens, battle UI

For simplicity and reliability, I'll implement canvas for the overworld and battle sprites, and DOM for UI overlays. World map: tile grid, 8 biome zones laid out in a big contiguous map (e.g., 120x120 tiles) with hand-crafted-ish generation seeded. Smooth pixel movement with collision. Camera follow. Wild monsters visible as roaming entities; interacting/approaching triggers encounter.

Could also do DOM-based battle screen for polish, with canvas monster sprites inside. Battle animations with CSS.

Asset-less art: generate pixel sprites via deterministic monster archetype drawing on a small offscreen canvas (e.g., 32x32) with palettes, body shapes, ears/horns/wings/tails, eyes. Evolution variants change size/accessories. This can look decent if designed carefully.

World tiles drawn via canvas with procedural patterns. Need attractive world: grass/dirt/water/lava/snow/crystal/swamp/ruins/dragon/celestial. Use tile types per biome plus transitions? Simpler: big world divided into 8 biome regions with path network; each region drawn with theme colors and decorations. Add landmark buildings, NPCs.

Let me consider scale of effort and token budget. We have plenty but must be efficient. Aim ~4000-6000 lines across files.

Plan files:

```
index.html
styles.css
src/main.js
src/core/utils.js
src/core/save.js
src/core/audio.js (maybe simple WebAudio SFX)
src/data/elements.js
src/data/skills.js
src/data/monsters.js
src/data/items.js
src/data/biomes.js
src/data/quests.js
src/data/npcs.js
src/game/state.js
src/game/monsters.js (factory, xp, stats, evolution)
src/game/capture.js
src/game/battle.js
src/game/world.js
src/game/inventory.js
src/game/breeding.js
src/render/sprites.js
src/render/world.js
src/ui/screens.js
src/ui/battle.js
src/ui/hud.js
src/ui/common.js
```

Maybe consolidate some to reduce cross-file complexity. No build step, ES modules served statically.

Key design decisions:

1. Map: tile grid 160x110? Each biome occupies a zone. Let me design map with regions arranged in a 3x3 grid-ish:

- Greenwood Forest (top-left)
- Ember Volcano (top-right)
- Frozen Mountains (top-center/right?)
- Crystal Desert (center-right)
- Shadow Swamp (bottom-left)
- Ancient Ruins (center-left)
- Dragon Valley (bottom-right)
- Celestial Island (top-center? isolated by water with bridge)

Interconnected with roads. Maybe use a big map 144x108, with regions defined by rectangles and blended terrain. Use graph paths with carved roads. Place towns/outposts per biome with NPCs, healer, shop, storage.

Simpler robust approach: define biome centers and assign tile type based on nearest biome center (Voronoi) with smooth boundaries + roads along edges between centers. Then sea surrounding map; celestial island accessed via bridge? Could allow travel via gate/portal to island, but "interconnected world" – make Celestial Island in top-right corner separated by water with a bridge path.

Actually a Voronoi with 8 seeds in a 3x3 layout gives nice organic regions. Height/noise variation. Map 150x110 tiles at 16px = 2400x1760 world pixels. Camera decent.

Tile types:
- grass, darkgrass, forest (tree obstacles), water, sand, snow, ice, lava, ashland, swamp, crystal, ruinfloor, rock, path, flower.
Walkable vs blocked.

Collision: tile blocked check + object collision (NPCs, buildings, wild monsters handled separately).

Wild monsters: spawn dynamically per biome on walkable tiles, roaming with simple AI; visible sprites; on approach (distance < 24px) or interact (E/space/tap) start encounter. Max ~12 active spawns; respawn. Level scaling per region.

Player movement: WASD/arrows, joystick on mobile (DOM joystick), smooth velocity + collision. Run with shift. Interaction prompt.

Encounters: approach triggers battle transition. Requirement says wild monsters appear in world, start encounters when approach. I'll trigger when within ~20px, with a small grace.

Battle system: DOM overlay with arena, turn order based on speed. Player actions:
- Attack (basic)
- Skills (4 slots, MP/energy? Use "SP" or stamina). Skills with power, element, status, effects.
- Switch (party)
- Items (capture orbs, potions)
- Escape (chance based on speed)

Element chart: 8 elements (Nature, Flame, Frost, Terra, Shadow, Light, Storm, Arcane?) Match themes: Verdant/Nature, Ember/Flame, Frost, Crystal/Earth, Shadow, Ancient/Arcane, Dragon, Celestial/Light, plus Storm? Keep 8: Nature, Flame, Frost, Earth, Shadow, Light, Storm, Dragon. Each monster 1 element (maybe dual for higher evolutions). Effectiveness chart.

Capture probability: based on current HP ratio, rarity, status (sleep/frozen/paralysis boost), orb quality, level diff, capture difficulty. Show percentage in UI.

Status effects: burn, freeze, poison, sleep, paralysis, buff/debuff.

Stats: monster instance with level, xp, personality (stat multipliers), friendship, skills unlocked by level, passive. IVs? Keep simple: base stats + personality + level. Evolution at thresholds/items/friendship/location; multiple paths.

Persistence: localStorage save, autosave periodically + on key events, manual save in menu.

Progression: player trainer level from achievements/badges? Trainer XP from battles, level, unlocks. Achievements tracked.

Quests: quest data with objectives (catch N, defeat boss, collect items, evolve, visit biome), journal UI with tracking and rewards. Implement event system.

Crafting: recipes from resources gathered in world (nodes like herbs, ore, crystals, embers, ice shards, etc.) craft orbs, potions. Inventory UI with use/craft tabs. Gathering by interacting with resource nodes.

Breeding: at Ancient Ruins nursery NPC; select two party monsters, produce egg based on species, inherit skill/personality; egg hatches after steps. Could implement egg item with steps count.

NPC trainers: static trainers with parties; interact to battle; rewards money. Regional bosses: special boss wild monster per biome, high level, respawn daily/never; defeating gives achievement and unique capture opportunity.

Day/night: world tint overlay; spawn tables change at night; clock UI; time advances with steps and real-time, rest at camp changes time.

UI screens: main menu (title screen with Start/Continue/Settings), HUD, party, monster details, storage, pokedex, inventory, map (minimap/full map), quest journal, achievements, settings, shop, breeding, evolution modal, battle UI.

Polished styling: pixel font via Google Fonts? Offline perhaps no network; use CSS font stack with monospace, and maybe embed "Press Start 2P" via Google Fonts link (may fail offline but fallback). Better use system font with pixel-esque styling? Could include a custom pixel font via base64? Too heavy. Use Google Fonts link with fallback to monospace; screenshots environment likely has network. We can use "Silkscreen" or "Press Start 2P" for headings and "Outfit" for body? The capture environment may be offline. Test. Prefer local: use monospace + letterspacing. I'll include Google Fonts link but ensure fallback looks fine. Maybe skip remote fonts to avoid delays. I'll use 'Segoe UI'? Pixel look through borders, shadows. Let me use CSS `font-family: 'Courier New'`? Hmm. I can generate/ship a tiny pixel font using canvas? Overkill. Use Google Font "Press Start 2P" for display and "Nunito" body with fallbacks. If offline, fallback to monospace/sans.

Rendering: main canvas for world + battle? Battle can use canvas for sprites in DOM. Use one canvas for overworld; monster sprite canvases rendered as data URLs/canvas elements.

Pixel sprites: Generate 32x32/40x40 pixel-art from species definitions:
- body type: quadruped, biped, bird, serpent, blob, insect, dragon, golem, spirit
- palette from seed
- features: horns, wings, tails, ears, crest, spikes, eyes count
- Draw with pixel grid primitives on 32x32 canvas, upscale with image-rendering:pixelated.

Need distinct recognizable monsters. Could author 60 monster definitions with variant params. Procedural generator with ~10 body archetypes and features yields variety. Evolution stage changes size/features.

Also wild overworld sprites 16x16 versions rendered from same generator, animated bob.

Battle monster sprites bigger (canvas 64 with scale 3-4), animate idle/attack/hit via CSS transforms.

Let me start building.

First set up package? Plain static html, no package needed. Start server via `node $RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs` or python http server. For local testing, use `python3 -m http.server 3002`. Screenshots via playwright-cli or custom node script. Check playwright availability.

export const MONSTER_LIST = Object.values(MONSTERS)
export const STARTERS = ['sprigling', 'cindercub', 'snowpup']
export const LEGENDARIES = MONSTER_LIST.filter(m => m.legendary)

export function getMonster(id) {
  return MONSTERS[id] || MONSTERS.sprigling
}

// Evolution helpers ---------------------------------------------------------
export function evolutionOptions(monster, biome = null) {
  const species = getMonster(monster.speciesId)
  if (!species.evolutions) return []
  return species.evolutions.filter(evo => {
    switch (evo.type) {
      case 'level': return monster.level >= evo.level
      case 'item': return monster.level >= (evo.level || 1)
      case 'friendship': return monster.level >= (evo.level || 1) && monster.friendship >= (evo.friendship || 70)
      case 'location': return monster.level >= (evo.level || 1) && (!biome || biome === evo.biome)
      default: return false
    }
  })
}

export function baseSpeciesId(speciesId) {
  // Walk backwards to the first evolution stage (used by breeding).
  let current = getMonster(speciesId)
  let guard = 0
  while (guard++ < 10) {
    const parent = MONSTER_LIST.find(m => m.evolutions.some(e => e.to === current.id))
    if (!parent) return current.id
    current = parent
  }
  return current.id
}

Stat stages reset per battle; store separate `stages` per active monster via map uid→stages? When switching, stages reset. Keep battle.combatant objects:
```

enemySide...
```
On switch, new combatant state.

Turn flow: player selects action. Build actions:
- action types: move, switch, item, escape, capture.
- Player action and enemy AI action; determine priority and speed. Items/switch happen first (priority 6), escape priority 5. Moves priority skill.priority or 0.
- Execute action events sequentially. Between each, check fainted.
- End-of-turn status effects (burn/poison/seed) for both.
- Faint handling: if enemy faints → award xp to player active (and maybe all participating) and level ups; if more enemy party (trainer), AI sends next; if none → victory.
- if player active faints → force switch selection (UI). Battle pauses awaiting switch. Return events with `mustSwitch:true`.
- Escape: wild only; chance based on speeds; trainer battle disabled. On success end battle escaped.
- Capture: wild/boss/mythic only (trainers no). Compute chance, roll, event sequence; on success add to party/storage; battle ends. Capture can only target active enemy. Capture items used → UI calls action {type:'capture', itemId}. Boss capture maybe allowed (requirements regional boss monsters; nice), mythic allowed low.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D monster-catcher RPG, starting with a tested core prototype featuring exploration, wild encounters, catching, party management, turn-based battles, and persistent progress.

## Requirements
- Original pixel-art fantasy world with eight biomes, original monsters, exploration, capture, combat, training, evolution, quests, and progression.
- Responsive PC and mobile controls/UI; persistent save/load; functional interactions and modular code.
- Start by implementing and testing player movement, a small explorable map, encounters, catching, party management, and battles; expand afterward.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; briefly note assumptions when finished.

## Decisions
- Assistant chose a static vanilla JavaScript app with no build step, using canvas for gameplay and DOM for UI.
- World and monster sprites are procedurally generated.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created foundational data modules for elements, skills, passives, monsters, items, biomes, quests, NPCs, and personalities.
- Implemented core utilities, monster creation/progression/evolution logic, persistent state, quests/achievements, inventory actions, procedural sprites, world generation/rendering, and a turn-based battle engine.
- Began shared UI primitives and HUD.

### Active
- Build the remaining UI and connect the systems into a playable game.
- Test gameplay systems and fix issues; no testing or browser verification has been reported yet.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the existing files and finish the UI screens, app entry point, HTML, and CSS.
2. Connect player controls, world interactions, encounters, catching, party/storage, combat, and save/load.
3. Run the app and test core gameplay; fix runtime or interaction issues.
4. Report assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/data/`: Game databases, including monsters, skills, items, biomes, quests, and NPCs.
- `src/core/`: Utilities and event bus.
- `src/game/`: Monster, state, world, progression, inventory, and battle systems.
- `src/render/`: Procedural sprites and world renderer.
- `src/ui/common.js`: Shared UI components.
- `src/ui/hud.js`: In-game HUD.

## Important Context
- The assistant described the repository as empty and started a static vanilla JS implementation.
- No final playable build, test results, or screenshot checks have been produced.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D monster-catcher RPG with exploration, encounters, catching, battles, party management, and persistent progress.

## Requirements
- Create an original pixel-art fantasy world with eight biomes, monsters, quests, combat, training, evolution, and progression.
- Support PC and mobile controls/UI, save/load, and functional interactions.
- Start with a tested core prototype; expand after the core is playable.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; briefly note assumptions when finished.
- Save the code on GitHub before reaching the limit.

## Decisions
- Use a static vanilla JavaScript app with no build step, canvas gameplay, and DOM UI.
- Generate world and monster sprites procedurally.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented foundational data, core utilities, monster progression, state persistence, quests, inventory, procedural sprites, world rendering, battle engine, shared UI primitives, and HUD.
- Added extensive party, storage, monster detail, codex, bag, map, quest, menu/settings, NPC, shop, and breeding screens in `src/ui/screens.js`.
- Committed initial work as `be4391a` (`Build 2D monster catcher RPG: data, engine, world and UI foundations`) and pushed the branch to GitHub.

### Active
- Finish the remaining UI and app entry point, then connect screens to movement, encounters, catching, combat, and save/load.
- Run and verify the playable game; no tests or browser verification have been reported.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the repository and `src/ui/screens.js`; determine what UI, HTML, and CSS remain unfinished.
2. Connect player controls, world interactions, encounters, catching, party/storage, combat, and save/load.
3. Run the app, test core gameplay, and fix runtime or interaction issues.
4. Commit and push subsequent changes to GitHub; report assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/ui/screens.js`: Newly added UI screens; created after the initial commit.
- `src/ui/common.js`: Shared UI components.
- `src/ui/hud.js`: In-game HUD.
- `src/game/`: Game systems for state, world, monsters, inventory, progression, and battles.
- `src/render/`: Procedural sprites and world renderer.
- `src/data/`: Game databases, including monsters, skills, items, biomes, quests, and NPCs.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.
- `startup.sh`: Additional startup script.

## Important Context
- The initial foundations were committed and pushed, but `src/ui/screens.js` was created afterward and is uncommitted.
- No final playable build or test results have been reported.

messages.text:
"Project: 2D Monster Catcher RPG

Create a complete 2D Monster Catcher RPG with an original fantasy world, original monsters, exploration, monster capturing, training, evolution, and turn-based combat.

1. Game Style

- 2D top-down RPG.
- Pixel art visual style.
- Smooth character movement and animations.
- Large interconnected world.
- Support PC and mobile controls.
- Responsive UI.

2. World Exploration

Create an explorable world containing multiple biomes:

- Greenwood Forest
- Ember Volcano
- Frozen Mountains
- Crystal Desert
- Shadow Swamp
- Ancient Ruins
- Dragon Valley
- Celestial Island

Each biome must have unique monsters, resources, NPCs, quests, and environmental designs.

3. Monster System

Create a monster database containing at least 50 original monsters initially.

Every monster must have:

- Unique ID and name.
- Sprite and animations.
- Element and rarity.
- Level and experience.
- HP, Attack, Defense, Speed, Special Attack and Special Defense.
- Skills and passive abilities.
- Evolution stages.
- Capture difficulty.
- Biome spawn information.

4. Catching System

- Wild monsters appear in the world.
- Start encounters when the player interacts with or approaches wild monsters.
- Allow the player to weaken monsters.
- Use capture items to catch monsters.
- Calculate capture probability using HP, rarity, status effects and capture item quality.
- Show capture animations and feedback.
- Add a monster storage system.

5. Combat System

Implement turn-based combat with:

- Attack.
- Skills.
- Monster switching.
- Items.
- Escape from wild battles.
- Elemental strengths and weaknesses.
- Critical hits.
- Status effects.
- Experience and rewards.

Allow the player to carry six monsters in the active party.

6. Evolution System

- Monsters can evolve into stronger forms.
- Add level-based evolution.
- Add item-based evolution.
- Add friendship-based evolution.
- Add location-based evolution.
- Evolution changes appearance, stats and abilities.
- Allow multiple evolution paths where appropriate.

7. Progression

Implement:

- Monster leveling.
- Experience rewards.
- Skill unlocking.
- Passive abilities.
- Monster personalities.
- Quests and achievements.
- Trainer progression.

8. Additional Systems

- Pokédex.
- Monster storage.
- Inventory.
- Crafting.
- Breeding.
- NPC trainers.
- Regional boss monsters.
- Day and night cycle.
- Save and load system.

9. UI

Create polished interfaces for:

- Main menu.
- Party.
- Monster details.
- Monster storage.
- Pokédex.
- Inventory.
- Map.
- Quest journal.
- Battle screen.
- Settings.

10. Development Requirements

- Use modular, maintainable code.
- Separate monster data from gameplay logic.
- Use reusable monster and battle systems.
- Avoid duplicating code.
- Implement proper collision detection.
- Ensure smooth movement and transitions.
- Save player progress persistently.
- Make all buttons and gameplay systems functional.

IMPORTANT:
Do not create just a visual prototype. Build actual playable systems with working interactions, progression, and persistent game data.

Start by creating the core playable prototype: player movement, a small explorable map, wild monster encounters, monster catching, party management, and turn-based battles. Test each system before expanding the game.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D monster-catcher RPG with exploration, original monsters, capturing, training, evolution, turn-based combat, and persistent progress.

## Requirements
- Top-down pixel-art RPG with smooth movement, interconnected biomes, responsive PC/mobile support, and functional UI.
- Include eight biomes: Greenwood Forest, Ember Volcano, Frozen Mountains, Crystal Desert, Shadow Swamp, Ancient Ruins, Dragon Valley, and Celestial Island.
- Create at least 50 original monsters with unique identities, stats, skills, passives, sprites, and animations.
- Implement quests, NPCs, resources, inventory, party/storage, catching, battles, training, evolution, progression, and save/load.
- Build and test a playable core; do not deliver only a visual prototype.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Use a static vanilla JavaScript app with no build step, canvas gameplay, and DOM UI.
- Generate world and monster sprites procedurally.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented foundational data, game utilities, monster progression, persistence, quests, inventory, procedural sprites, world rendering, battle engine, shared UI primitives, and HUD.
- Added extensive party, storage, monster detail, codex, bag, map, quest, menu/settings, NPC, shop, and breeding screens in `src/ui/screens.js`.
- Committed and pushed initial work as `be4391a` (`Build 2D monster catcher RPG: data, engine, world and UI foundations`).

### Active
- Complete the app entry point and remaining UI, then connect screens to movement, encounters, catching, combat, and save/load.
- Run and verify gameplay; no tests or browser verification have been reported.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the repository and `src/ui/screens.js` to identify unfinished UI, HTML, and CSS.
2. Connect player controls, world interactions, encounters, catching, party/storage, combat, and persistence.
3. Run the app and test core gameplay; fix runtime or interaction issues.
4. Commit and push subsequent changes to GitHub; report assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `src/ui/screens.js`: UI screens added after the initial commit; currently uncommitted.
- `src/ui/common.js`: Shared UI components.
- `src/ui/hud.js`: In-game HUD.
- `src/game/`: Game systems for state, world, monsters, inventory, progression, and battles.
- `src/render/`: Procedural sprites and world renderer.
- `src/data/`: Databases for monsters, skills, items, biomes, quests, and NPCs.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.
- `startup.sh`: Additional startup script.

## Important Context
- The initial foundations are committed and pushed; `src/ui/screens.js` was added afterward and is uncommitted.
- No completed playable build or verification results have been reported.
